# PanelKit

> Laravel + Vue + Inertia administration framework. Resources, tables, forms and
> infolists are declared as PHP classes; a Vue kit renders them over Inertia. Not
> Filament, not Livewire - do not assume Filament conventions or property names.

Canonical documentation: https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/
AI coding agents: read https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/ai/ (or AI_BLUEPRINT.md in the repository root) before generating PanelKit code.
Full documentation corpus: https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/llms-full.txt

## Getting started

- [What is PanelKit?](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/): PanelKit is a schema-driven administration framework for Laravel. You describe a screen — a list, a form, a detail view — as a single PHP class. The panel turns that description into a route, a naviga
- [Architecture](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/architecture): 1. **Discovery.** A `Resource` subclass sitting in a discovered directory (`app/Panel/Resources` by default) is found at boot — nothing is registered by hand. 2. **Schema.** `table()`/`form()`/`infoli
- [Your first resource](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/first-resource): This walks through building a `Customer` resource from a plain Eloquent model, by hand, so each generated piece is understood rather than taken on faith. If you just want a working screen immediately,
- [Installation](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/installation): PanelKit installs from GitHub via a Composer VCS repository. There is no Packagist package and no npm registry package.
- [Philosophy](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/philosophy): A handful of decisions run through every part of PanelKit. Knowing them makes the rest of the framework predictable instead of memorized.
- [Project structure](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/project-structure): After `panel:install`, a fresh application gains:
- [Quick start](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/quick-start): After [installing](/getting-started/installation), the fastest way to see a real, working screen is the official starter recipe — not a hand-written resource, so you're looking at a known-good baselin
- [Requirements](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/getting-started/requirements): - PHP 8.4 - Laravel 12 or 13 - Inertia 2 or 3 - Vue 3.5 - Node.js only if you customise the Vue kit and run your own build — see [Installation](/getting-started/installation)

## Resources

- [Creating resources](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/resources/): A `Resource` is one PHP class that declares everything about a model's admin screens: its table, its form, its navigation identity, its lifecycle hooks, and (optionally) its own infolist. Nothing abou
- [Global search](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/resources/global-search): Every resource participates in the panel's command-palette-style search by default, ranked by `recordTitle()` and a handful of per-resource overrides — no separate search index or configuration is req
- [Nested resources](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/resources/nested-resources): A nested resource is a **full, independent `Resource`** that only answers under its parent's URL — distinct from a [RelationManager](/relation-managers/), which is a tab on the parent's own page. Reac
- [Singular resources](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/resources/singular-resources): A `SingularResource` is a form and two functions — no list, no create screen, no hand-written controller. Use it for a "one record, no list" screen: a settings page, a company profile, anything where 

## Authentication

- [Authentication](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/authentication/): PanelKit does not require a particular auth stack. Breeze, Jetstream, Fortify or your own are all ordinary consumers — every feature below degrades honestly when its dependency is absent (a Security s
- [MFA & passwordless](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/authentication/mfa): Two independent factors both land on one challenge screen after a correct password (or a matched social login — **social sign-in is never a 2FA bypass**): TOTP with recovery codes, and email OTP. If b
- [Registration & email verification](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/authentication/registration): Both are off until explicitly enabled — a fresh install assumes operators are invited, not self-registered.
- [Social sign-in](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/authentication/social): Requires `laravel/socialite` (a Composer suggest, not a hard dependency) — without it, the buttons stay hidden and nothing 500s.
- [Turnstile](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/authentication/turnstile): Cloudflare Turnstile is fully built into PanelKit and genuinely optional — off by default, on only once you provide keys.

## Forms

- [Form schema & layout](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/): `Form::schema()` declares a resource's create/edit form as a tree of layout nodes and fields — the layout is data too, cached the same way `table()` is.
- [Checkboxes & toggles](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/checkboxes-and-toggles): `CheckboxField` and `ToggleField` are functionally identical — same `boolean` validation rule, same behavior — and differ only in which control fits the surrounding form visually. Both share a detail 
- [Custom fields](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/custom-fields): Before writing one, check the [full field catalogue](/forms/#every-field-type) — 34 field types already ship, covering nearly everything an ordinary CRUD screen needs. Reach for a custom field only wh
- [Dates](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/dates): `withTime()` toggles the field between `date` and `datetime` — both are the same `DateField` class; there's no separate `DateTimeField`. On the display side, [`DateColumn`](/tables/#money-badges-dates
- [Numbers & money](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/numbers-and-money): `NumberField` is integer-only by design — it exists specifically so decimal amounts have to go through `MoneyField` instead of an easily-misused generic number input. `presets()` adds decision chips; 
- [Selects & relationships](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/selects-and-relationships): `relationship()` takes a related model class and the **attribute name on that model** to search and display — not a dotted relationship path. It:
- [Textarea, markdown, rich text, code](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/text-content): Four fields cover "more than a line of text," each storing something different — picking the wrong one means picking the wrong storage shape later.
- [Text fields](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/text-fields): `PhoneField` validates against an E.164-shaped pattern (`/^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/`) — a leading `+`, country code, no spaces or punctuation. If your application accepts locally-formatted numbers, normalize
- [Uploads](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/uploads): Uploads are **two-phase**: the file itself goes to its own upload endpoint first, and the form only ever carries a path/handle string — not the file bytes. This is why `typeRules()` validates the hand
- [Validation](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/forms/validation): Most fields derive their own base rules from their *type* (`typeRules()`) — a `NumberField` is always at least `integer`, a `DateField` is always at least `date` — before any `->rule()` calls you add 

## Tables

- [Columns](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/tables/): `Table::columns()` declares a resource's list screen. Search, sort persistence, pagination, column visibility, density, saved views, selection, export and the empty state all come with the table for f

## Infolists

- [Infolists & View pages](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/infolists/): An infolist declares a resource's dedicated View page — independently of what the List page's table shows.

## Relation Managers

- [Relation Managers](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/relation-managers/): A `RelationManager` is a tab of related records on a parent's own record page — distinct from a [nested resource](/resources/nested-resources), which is a full, independently-routed `Resource` reachab
- [Capability comparison](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/relation-managers/capability-comparison): The row that usually decides it: **searchable relationship fields**. If the related form needs a `SelectField` that searches (rather than a small fixed `options()` list), the simple shape refuses to b
- [Example: Order → OrderItems → Product](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/relation-managers/example-orders): A complete, realistic use of a resource-backed RelationManager: an `Order` that lists its `OrderItem` rows, each pointing at a `Product` through a searchable relationship field — exactly the combinati
- [Resource-backed RelationManager](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/relation-managers/resource-backed): `->resource()` points the tab at a **full, independently-routed nested `Resource`** — see [Nested resources](/resources/nested-resources) for that class's own `$parent`/`$parentColumn`/`$relationship`
- [Simple RelationManager](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/relation-managers/simple): `related()` names the child model and its foreign key column. `table()` and `form()` each take a closure, exactly like a `Resource`'s own `table()`/ `form()` methods. `authorize()` checks an ability *

## Actions

- [Actions](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/actions/): PanelKit has three action-shaped classes that are easy to confuse — they share vocabulary (`make()`, `authorize()`, `icon()`) but serve different places in the UI:
- [Bulk actions](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/actions/bulk-actions): A [`BulkAction`](/api/classes/bulk-action) runs against a selection rather than a single record. Like `RecordAction`, it has two shapes:
- [Forms inside actions](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/actions/forms-in-actions): Most real actions need a value before they can do anything — a reason, an amount, a plan, a department. `->form()` collects it inline, without writing a dedicated screen for a one-field prompt.
- [Record actions](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/actions/record-actions): A [`RecordAction`](/api/classes/record-action) is a row-menu action or a View-page action. It has three mutually distinct shapes — pick one:

## Authorization

- [Authorization](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/authorization/): Two independent gates, and both must pass on every request: **tenancy** asks *is this yours*, **permission** asks *may you do this to it*. Full permissions still can't reach another organisation's rec

## Navigation

- [Navigation](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/navigation/): A resource, page, or cluster's place in the sidebar comes from three static properties: `$icon`, `$group`, `$sort`.

## Money

- [Money](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/money/): Money is the field type most likely to be silently wrong: a mismatch between storage and display doesn't crash anything, it just makes every amount on screen ten or a hundred times too big or too smal

## Customization

- [Customization](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/customization/): PanelKit ships a small, deliberately frozen set of layout tokens. Screens that look inconsistent are almost always screens that invented a second layout system instead of reaching for the shared one.

## Extending PanelKit

- [Extending PanelKit](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/extending/): Most application work is building *with* PanelKit's existing Fields, Columns, Entries, Actions and Pages, not writing new ones. Check the existing catalogues first — [Forms](/forms/), [Tables](/tables
- [Custom columns & entries](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/extending/custom-columns-and-entries): Columns and entries share the same underlying mechanism as [custom fields](/forms/custom-fields), applied to the List and View pages respectively.
- [Custom pages](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/extending/custom-pages): Not every screen is a list of records. A `Page` is one PHP class plus a Vue file, for anything else — a settings screen, an operational dashboard, a tool.
- [Plugins](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/extending/plugins): A `PanelPlugin` bundles resources, pages, widgets, navigation entries, and render-hook markup into one reusable, installable unit — for your own first-party packages shared across projects, not a thir
- [Vue extension points](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/extending/vue-extension-points): Three module-scope registries in the client package are how PHP-declared schema types resolve to actual Vue components. There is no `registerColumn` or `registerAction` — only these three.

## Commands

- [Command reference](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/commands/): Every command below is a real `$signature` read directly from `packages/panel/src/Commands/*.php`. If a flag isn't listed here, it doesn't exist — don't guess one into existence.

- [Production checklist](https://alxtexh.github.io/panelkit/deployment/): Bulk actions past the queue threshold, exports, imports, and scheduled reports all dispatch jobs. Without a worker running, they queue and never run — the screen reports a job stuck pending, not an er
